scope: Local reproduction and verification of the WASIX coroutine C-stack defect on PR #2 branch content. Not a Linux boot, snapshot/restore or Edge test.

toolchain.wasmer: 7.5.0 (bin/wasmer from wasix-org llvm-project 21.1.206 release, run via nix glibc loader)
toolchain.note: Toolchain installed locally for this repro; binaries are upstream release artifacts, not built from source here.

defect: WASIX contexts do not receive separate linear-memory C stacks: N concurrently suspended coroutines consume one shared guest stack until it leaves the -z stack-size region (no native guard pages on this target).
not_reproduced: Byte-level clobbering of a suspended context’s stack data (the gist’s 255/256 observation) did not reproduce with a 2-context A→B→A probe on this exact toolchain; guards stayed intact in every run.

tests.coroutine_stack_test: ports/wasix/test-coroutine-stack.c driven through ports/wasix/coroutine-wasix.c with QEMU enter/yield/terminate protocol; 16 KiB address-taken frame + 256-byte guard per coroutine; all coroutines suspended before any resume

results_before.outcome: TRAP RuntimeError: out of bounds memory access at worker_entry / coroutine_trampoline
TRAP RuntimeError: out of bounds memory access

tests.shim_validation: sp-shim-test.c: callee frame landed inside the supplied 64 KiB region (in_region:1), caller SP restored (0x501e9c before/after), indirect call returned 42

capability_gate.command: clang --target=wasm32-wasixp1 (21.1.2) + sysroot v2026-10-02.1, wasmer run ports/wasix/capabilities.c build
capability_gate.output: fresh-instance PASS, pthread PASS, pipe PASS, context PASS, memory_pages 1105, exit 0 on two instances; loop mode killed by 3 s supervisor deadline (rc 124)

caveats: No full QEMU build was run in this environment, so the util/meson.build wiring for the .S is unverified.
Aggregate cgroup memory is 3 GiB on the test host; the guard is session-wide, not engine-isolated.
